name: continuum-retrieval-v1
description: Synthetic, controlled memory corpus for comparing Continuum retrieval pipelines. Memories 1-3 are the original manual test memories; the rest are invented but realistic. Several memories are deliberate hard negatives that share words with a query without answering it.
labeling_rule: A memory is relevant if it directly answers, or directly supports the answer to, the query. Sharing a topic or a word is not enough. Queries in no_answer_queries have no relevant memory in the corpus and are used only to inspect score calibration.

memories.content: I joined Infor as an AI Developer Intern in FEBRUARY 2026.
I want to pursue my Masters in Germany.
I enjoy playing football on weekends.
My manager at work is Priya, and we have a one-on-one every Thursday afternoon.
At work I'm building an internal document question-answering assistant using retrieval-augmented generation.
My internship contract runs until January 2027, and there might be a full-time offer after that.
I go into the office three days a week and work from home on Mondays and Fridays.
My friend Rahul works as a backend engineer at Infosys.
In summer 2025 I did an internship building Power BI dashboards for a small analytics startup.
My team's standup meeting is at 10 AM every weekday.
I'm in the final year of my B.Tech in Computer Science and will graduate in May 2027.
My current CGPA is 8.4 out of 10.
I'm shortlisting TU Munich, RWTH Aachen and TU Berlin for a Masters in Data Science or Artificial Intelligence.
I need an IELTS score of at least 7.0 for my German university applications.
I booked my IELTS exam for 15 November 2026.
I'm learning German on Duolingo and I'm roughly at A1 level.
I still have to apply for the APS certificate, which Indian students need before applying to German universities.
I'm aiming for the winter semester 2027 intake for my Masters.
My cousin did his Masters at TU Dresden and now works in Munich.
I have to submit my final-year project proposal to my college by 10 October 2026.
My younger sister is preparing for NEET because she wants to study medicine.
To get a German student visa I need to deposit about 11,904 euros in a blocked account.
I'm saving part of my internship stipend every month to fund my Masters.
I play as a left winger in a five-a-side league on Saturday evenings.
I support FC Barcelona and try to watch their matches live.
I go to the gym on Tuesday and Thursday mornings.
I want to run a half marathon sometime in 2027.
I usually read sci-fi novels before bed; right now I'm reading Project Hail Mary.
I'm vegetarian and I don't eat eggs.
I'm allergic to peanuts.
I drink black coffee, but never after 6 PM because it ruins my sleep.
I try to be asleep by 11:30 PM on weeknights.
I live with my parents and take the metro to the office, which takes about 40 minutes.
I speak English, Hindi and Telugu.
I promised to review Rahul's resume this weekend.
I need to renew my passport before it expires in March 2027.
Continuum is my side project: a local-first AI memory system that stores my personal and project context.
The long-term vision for Continuum is a context-transfer layer, so context from one LLM can be packaged and handed to a different LLM.
Continuum's backend is built with FastAPI, SQLModel and PostgreSQL.
Continuum uses JWT authentication with the OAuth2 password flow, and every memory is scoped to its owner.
PostgreSQL is the source of truth for memories in Continuum; ChromaDB is only a derived index that can be rebuilt.
I recreated the Chroma collection with cosine distance and reindexed all memories from PostgreSQL.
Continuum embeds memories locally with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5.
Continuum's local LLM is Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct running on the GPU.
I lowered the semantic similarity threshold from 0.5 to 0.4 because 0.5 was dropping relevant memories.
I added BM25 keyword search and Reciprocal Rank Fusion to Continuum as retrieval prototypes.
The bge-reranker-base cross-encoder put the wrong memory first on some work questions, so it isn't in the main pipeline yet.
ContextPackage is Continuum's provider-independent format with project, objective, current state, decisions, constraints, relevant memories and open tasks.
My next Continuum task is building a retrieval evaluation set to measure Recall@k and MRR.
Later I want Continuum adapters that format a ContextPackage for ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.
I still need to write pytest tests for Continuum's memory ownership checks.
Continuum has an MCP server so other AI tools can query my memories.
I want to open-source Continuum on GitHub by the end of 2026.
I prefer running open-source Hugging Face models locally instead of paying for OpenAI or Anthropic APIs.
All my Hugging Face models are stored on the D: drive because my C: drive is almost full.
My laptop GPU is an RTX 3050 with only 6 GB of VRAM, so models much bigger than 3B parameters are impractical.
My laptop has 16 GB of RAM.
I fixed the WinError 1455 crash when loading CUDA libraries by moving a 16 GB pagefile to the D: drive.
I write Python with type hints and Google-style docstrings, and I keep routers, services and core modules separate.
I prefer small, focused git commits with conventional commit messages like feat(retrieval).
I avoid LangChain because it hides too much; I'd rather write the retrieval pipeline myself.
I develop on Windows 11 using VS Code.
Because of my internship, I can only work on Continuum late in the evenings on weekdays.
My career goal is to become a machine learning engineer working on retrieval and LLM systems.
I'm more comfortable with PyTorch than TensorFlow.
